subject: maths
title: Fractions
description: Learn fractions step by step: what a fraction is, equivalent fractions, simplifying, comparing, adding and subtracting, and fractions of amounts. Free practice with instant feedback for ages 9 to 14.
intro: Pizza slices, chocolate bars and shared sweets: fractions are everywhere. Work through the path one unit at a time and collect your stars.

units.title: What is a fraction?
units.blurb: Equal parts, and what the top and bottom numbers mean.

learn.p: A fraction is a part of a whole that has been cut into **equal** parts. This circle is cut into 4 equal parts and 1 part is shaded, so {1/4} of it is shaded.
In {3/4}, the bottom number (the **denominator**) tells you how many equal parts the whole is cut into. The top number (the **numerator**) tells you how many of those parts you have.
Split the line from 0 to 1 into 4 equal steps. Each step is {1/4}. The arrow is 1 step along, so it points to {1/4}.

questions.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
questions.hint: Count all the equal parts first: that's the bottom number. Then count the shaded parts: that's the top number.
questions.explain: There are 4 equal parts and 1 is shaded, so the answer is {1/4}.

questions.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
questions.hint: How many equal parts is the bar cut into altogether?
questions.explain: The bar has 5 equal parts and 3 are shaded: {3/5}.

questions.q: What fraction of the circle is shaded? Type it like 3/4.
questions.hint: Count all the slices, then count the shaded slices.

questions.q: In the fraction {7/10}, what does the 10 tell you?
options: The whole is cut into 10 equal parts
questions.hint: The 10 is the bottom number, the denominator.
questions.explain: The bottom number tells you how many equal parts the whole is cut into. The top number (7) tells you how many you have.

questions.q: A pizza is cut into 6 equal slices. Sam eats 1 slice. What fraction of the pizza did Sam eat?
questions.hint: The pizza has 6 equal slices. How many did Sam eat?
questions.explain: 1 slice out of 6 equal slices is {1/6}.

questions.q: What fraction is the arrow pointing to?
questions.hint: How many equal steps are there from 0 to 1? How many steps along is the arrow?
questions.explain: The line from 0 to 1 has 5 equal steps. The arrow is 3 steps along, so it points to {3/5}.

questions.q: This bar is cut into 9 equal parts and 4 are shaded. What fraction is **not** shaded?
questions.hint: Count the parts that are white.
questions.explain: 9 − 4 = 5 parts are not shaded, so the answer is {5/9}.

questions.q: Which fraction is equal to one whole?
questions.hint: If you have every one of the equal parts, how much do you have?
questions.explain: {6/6} means 6 parts out of 6: all of it. When the top and bottom are the same, the fraction is 1 whole. ({6/1} is 6 wholes!)

units.title: Equivalent fractions
units.blurb: Different fractions that are the same amount.

learn.p: All three bars have the same amount shaded. So {1/2} = {2/4} = {4/8}. Fractions that are the same amount are called **equivalent fractions**.
Multiply the top **and** the bottom by the same number, and you get an equivalent fraction. {2/3}: multiply both by 2 to get {4/6}.
If the top and the bottom can both be divided by the same number, the fraction stays the same size. {6/9}: divide both by 3 to get {2/3}.

questions.q: The two bars are the same length. Which fraction of the bottom bar is shaded?
questions.hint: Count the parts of the bottom bar, then the shaded parts.
questions.explain: The bottom bar has 6 parts and 3 are shaded: {3/6}. It's the same amount as {1/2}, so {1/2} = {3/6}.

questions.q: {1/3} is equal to how many sixths? Type the top number.
questions.hint: What do you multiply 3 by to get 6? Do the same to the top.
questions.explain: 3 × 2 = 6, so multiply the top by 2 too: 1 × 2 = 2. So {1/3} = {2/6}.

questions.q: {3/4} is equal to how many twelfths? Type the top number.
questions.hint: 4 × ? = 12. Multiply the top by the same number.

questions.q: Which fraction is equivalent to {2/5}?
questions.hint: Try multiplying the top and the bottom of {2/5} by 2.

questions.q: Which fraction is **not** equivalent to {1/2}?
questions.hint: A fraction equal to {1/2} has a top number that is exactly half of the bottom number.
questions.explain: 5 is half of 10, 4 is half of 8 and 6 is half of 12. But 3 is not half of 5, so {3/5} is not equal to {1/2}.

questions.q: {10/15} is equal to how many thirds? Type the top number.
questions.hint: 15 ÷ ? = 3. Divide the top by the same number.

questions.q: Mia says {2/3} = {3/4} because she added 1 to the top and to the bottom. Is she right?
options: No: you have to multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number
Yes: adding the same number keeps fractions equal
Yes: both fractions are less than 1
questions.hint: Try writing both fractions in twelfths.
questions.explain: Adding does not keep fractions equal. {2/3} = {8/12} but {3/4} = {9/12}, so they are different.

questions.q: {5/6} is equal to how many twenty-fourths? Type the top number.

units.title: Simplifying fractions
units.blurb: Write fractions in their simplest form.

learn.p: A fraction is in its **simplest form** when no whole number bigger than 1 divides both the top and the bottom. {4/8} is the same amount as {1/2}, and {1/2} is its simplest form.

Find a number that divides **both** the top and the bottom, and divide both by it. Keep going until you can't.
{12/18} → divide both by 2 → {6/9} → divide both by 3 → {2/3}.
Divide by the **highest common factor** (HCF) to do it in one step. The HCF of 12 and 18 is 6, so {12/18} = {2/3} straight away.

questions.q: Write {2/4} in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Both 2 and 4 can be divided by 2.

questions.q: Write {6/8} in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Which number divides both 6 and 8?
questions.explain: Divide both by 2: {6/8} = {3/4}. Nothing else divides 3 and 4, so we're done.

questions.q: Write {5/15} in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Look at the 5 times table.

questions.q: Write {9/12} in its simplest form.
questions.hint: 9 and 12 are both in the 3 times table.

questions.q: Write {8/20} in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Try dividing both by 4.

questions.q: Write {14/21} in its simplest form.
questions.hint: 14 and 21 are both in the 7 times table.

questions.q: Which fraction is already in its simplest form?
questions.hint: For each fraction, is there a number bigger than 1 that divides both the top and the bottom?
questions.explain: Nothing bigger than 1 divides both 7 and 9. The others simplify: {6/9} = {2/3}, {4/10} = {2/5}, {3/12} = {1/4}.

questions.q: Write {18/24} in its simplest form.
questions.hint: The HCF of 18 and 24 is 6.

questions.q: Challenge: write {24/36} in its simplest form.
questions.hint: You can divide by 12 in one go, or by smaller numbers a few times.

learn.p: When the bottom numbers are the same, the parts are the same size. Just compare the tops: {5/8} is bigger than {3/8}.
The bigger the bottom number, the **smaller** each part. So {1/3} is bigger than {1/5}.
Change both fractions to equivalent fractions with the **same** bottom number, then compare the tops. {2/3} = {8/12} and {3/4} = {9/12}, so {3/4} is bigger.

questions.q: Which is bigger: {4/7} or {6/7}?
questions.hint: The bottom numbers are the same, so compare the tops.
questions.explain: Sevenths are the same size, and 6 of them is more than 4 of them.

questions.q: Which is bigger: {1/4} or {1/6}?
questions.hint: Would you rather have one slice of a cake cut into 4, or into 6?
questions.explain: Cutting into 4 makes bigger pieces than cutting into 6, so {1/4} is bigger.

questions.q: Which is the smallest?
questions.hint: The tops are all 1. Which has the most parts?
questions.explain: All have top number 1. The biggest bottom number makes the smallest parts, so {1/10} is the smallest.

questions.q: Which is bigger: {2/3} or {3/5}?
questions.hint: Change both into fifteenths.

questions.q: Which is bigger: {3/4} or {6/8}?
questions.hint: Multiply the top and the bottom of {3/4} by 2.
questions.explain: {3/4} = {6/8}. They are equivalent, so they are the same size.

questions.q: Which fraction is bigger than {1/2}?
questions.hint: Half of 5 is 2.5. Is the top number more than half of the bottom number?
questions.explain: 3 is more than half of 5, so {3/5} is more than {1/2}. In the others the top is less than half of the bottom.

questions.q: Put these in order, smallest first.
questions.hint: Change them all into sixths.

questions.q: Leo ate {3/8} of a pizza. Ava ate {1/4} of the same pizza. Who ate more?
questions.hint: How many eighths is {1/4}?
questions.explain: {1/4} = {2/8}. Leo ate {3/8}, which is more than {2/8}.

units.title: Adding and subtracting fractions
units.blurb: Add and take away fractions, even with different bottom numbers.

learn.p:
Add (or take away) the top numbers. Keep the bottom number the same.
{2/7} + {3/7} = {5/7}
{1/4} + {1/4} = {2/4}, which is the same as {1/2}. It is **not** {2/8}: two quarters make a half.

First make the bottom numbers the same, using equivalent fractions. Then add the tops.
{1/2} + {1/4} = {2/4} + {1/4} = {3/4}

questions.hint: The bottoms are the same. Add the tops.
Take away the tops. Keep the bottom the same.
questions.explain: 5 − 2 = 3, so the answer is {3/9}. That simplifies to {1/3}, and either answer is right.

questions.hint: Add the tops. Keep the bottom as 8.
How many quarters is {1/2}?
Change {2/3} into sixths first.
Both 3 and 4 go into 12. Change both fractions into twelfths.

questions.q: Jo says {1/3} + {1/3} = {2/6}. What has Jo done wrong?
options: Jo added the bottom numbers. The answer is {2/3}
questions.hint: When the bottom numbers are the same, what happens to them?
questions.explain: The bottom number stays the same: {1/3} + {1/3} = {2/3}. ({2/6} is only {1/3}, so it can't be the total.)

questions.q: A cake is cut into 8 equal slices. Tom eats {3/8} of the cake and Zara eats {2/8}. What fraction of the cake is left?
questions.hint: First find how much they ate together. The whole cake is {8/8}.
questions.explain: Together they ate {5/8}. The whole cake is {8/8}, so {8/8} − {5/8} = {3/8} is left.

questions.hint: Write 1 whole as fifths.

units.title: Fractions of amounts
units.blurb: Find a fraction of a number, like {3/4} of 20.

learn.p: To find {1/4} of 12, share 12 into 4 equal groups. Each group has 3, so {1/4} of 12 = 3.

To find {3/4} of 12, find {1/4} first (that's 3), then take 3 of those groups: 3 × 3 = 9.
**Divide by the bottom, multiply by the top.**
What is {2/5} of £20? Divide by the bottom: 20 ÷ 5 = 4. Multiply by the top: 4 × 2 = 8. So it's £8.

questions.q: What is {1/2} of 10?
questions.hint: Share 10 into 2 equal groups.

questions.q: What is {1/3} of 18?
questions.hint: Share 18 into 3 equal groups.

questions.q: What is {1/5} of 35?
questions.hint: Divide by the bottom number.

questions.q: What is {2/3} of 12?
questions.hint: Find {1/3} of 12 first, then double it.

questions.q: What is {3/4} of 20?
questions.hint: Divide by 4, then multiply by 3.

questions.q: What is {3/10} of 50?
questions.hint: Find {1/10} of 50 first.

questions.q: A class has 30 children. {2/5} of them walk to school. How many children walk to school?
questions.hint: Find {1/5} of 30 first.

questions.q: A bag has 24 sweets. Ali eats {1/6} of them. How many sweets are left?
questions.hint: First find how many Ali eats, then take that away from 24.
questions.explain: {1/6} of 24 = 24 ÷ 6 = 4 sweets eaten. 24 − 4 = 20 sweets are left.

questions.q: What is {3/8} of £40? Type the number of pounds.
questions.hint: Divide 40 by 8, then multiply by 3.

questions.q: Challenge: {1/4} of a number is 7. What is the number?
questions.hint: If one quarter is 7, how much are all four quarters?
questions.explain: The whole is 4 quarters, so 7 × 4 = 28. Check: {1/4} of 28 = 28 ÷ 4 = 7.
